us-house.budget-law-tax: a budget law that reduced national tax revenue by about 1.25 percent of yearly economic output each year across ten years, chiefly by making permanent the lower tax rates on earnings and business income that had been set to expire, increasing the amount of inherited wealth exempt from tax, and creating deductions for tips and overtime pay until 2028
us-house.overdraft-rule-repeal: the repeal of a rule that would have limited the fees that large banks and credit unions charge on overdrawn accounts to a low fixed amount or to their cost. The regulator's figures show that about one in six households pay these fees
us-house.federal-bargaining-bill: a bill giving back the right to collective bargaining to national government employees at agencies where the head of government's orders had taken it away. Government data show the share of national government employees represented by a union dropped from about 56 to about 38 percent in the year the orders took effect

uk-commons.finance-law-2025: a finance law that increased tax rates on investment gains, applied sales tax to private school fees, increased the additional purchase tax on second homes, and replaced a rule allowing some long-term residents to avoid tax on income held abroad, adding about 0.15 percent of annual economic output to tax revenue by 2030
uk-commons.finance-law-2026: a finance law that holds income tax thresholds fixed for a further three years, increases tax rates on dividend, savings, and property income by 2 points, and extends inheritance tax to unused pension savings and to more farm and business assets, adding about 0.35 percent of annual economic output to tax revenue by 2030
uk-commons.employment-rights-law: a law that shields employees from unfair dismissal after six months of service rather than two years, makes sick pay due from the first day of illness, gives workers on variable hours a right to guaranteed hours, restricts dismissing staff and rehiring them on worse terms, and relaxes rules on union organizing and strikes. By the government's estimate, it gives new rights to about 60 percent of workers

de-bundestag.investment-tax-law: a law that lowers the tax rate on company profits by 5 points in stages from 2028 to 2032, from about 30 to about 25 percent including local taxes, and permits faster deduction of investment costs until 2027. Its cost, by the official estimate, is up to about 0.25 percent of annual economic output a year
de-bundestag.tax-amendment-law: a tax law that permanently lowered the sales tax on restaurant meals from 19 to 7 percent and increased the deduction for commuting costs. Its cost, by the official estimate, is about 0.1 percent of annual economic output a year
de-bundestag.procurement-pay-law: a law that obliges companies carrying out national government contracts above a set value to give their workers the pay and conditions of the applicable collective agreements. The government counted about 16,000 of these contracts a year

fr-assemblee.budget-2025: an annual budget, adopted without a vote on its text, that introduced a temporary surtax on the profits of about 400 companies with the highest revenue and a minimum tax rate of 20 percent on the top incomes, increasing tax revenue by about 0.3 percent of annual economic output
fr-assemblee.budget-2026: the following annual budget, likewise adopted without a vote on its text, that kept that surtax for a second year on fewer companies and introduced a 20 percent tax on luxury assets held through family holding companies. By an unofficial estimate, the surtax yields about 0.25 percent of annual economic output
fr-assemblee.wealth-floor-bill: a bill that sets a minimum yearly tax of 2 percent of wealth on fortunes larger than about 500 times the median household's wealth, approved by the lower chamber and voted down by the upper chamber. A legislative committee put its yield at about 0.1 percent of annual economic output, and its author at about 0.7 percent

ca-commons.income-tax-cut: a law that lowered the lowest income tax rate from 15 to 14 percent. Its cost, by the official estimate, is about 0.15 percent of annual economic output a year, and the amount saved rises with income up to the second bracket
ca-commons.budget-law-investment: a budget law that allows businesses to deduct the cost of new investment more quickly. Its cost, by the official estimate, is about 0.1 percent of annual economic output a year over five years

Its national platform, adopted before this period, promises to increase the tax rate on company profits from 21 to 28 percent, impose a minimum tax rate of 25 percent on billionaires, end the lower tax rate on investment gains for incomes above about 12 times the median household income, and raise no taxes on anyone earning less than about 5 times that median. During this period all of its legislators voted against the tax cuts in the budget law.

That platform also promises to raise the national minimum wage to at least about twice its current level and to pass a bill strengthening workers' organizing rights. During this period about two-thirds of its legislators in the lower chamber were cosponsors of a bill to raise the minimum wage by about 135 percent by 2030, and more than 90 percent cosponsored the organizing-rights bill.
